loop.top3_why: The plain mean of the full pool (strategy A) offers the most robust, stable performance across the three validation windows (0.700, 0.650, 0.700) and matches the dataset‑wide best strategy (median/trimmed_mean). The weighted inverse‑error approaches (B and C) show higher variance in the second window and risk overfitting to the limited three‑window validation set, which is precisely the risk highlighted in the diagnosis. Thus A is the safest choice for generalization.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate B has a noticeably higher validation score and worse performance in the third window, indicating over‑weighting of a few models that may not generalize. Candidate C, while slightly better in the third window, still relies on inverse‑error weighting that is sensitive to the unstable model ranking and could overfit to the validation windows. Both are therefore less robust than the plain mean approach.
